name: Physics
dimension: the governing constants of the claim

objects.label: Classical motion and fields
objects.text: PH.O.A1 Classical motion and fields

objects.label: Particle mechanics
objects.text: PH.O.A1.1 Particle mechanics. Newton's laws hold in inertial frames for speeds much below c.

objects.label: Lagrangian and Hamiltonian mechanics are equivalent where the Legendre
objects.text: PH.O.A1.1.1 Lagrangian and Hamiltonian mechanics are equivalent where the Legendre transform is regular.

objects.label: Liouville's theorem
objects.text: PH.O.A1.1.2 Liouville's theorem: Hamiltonian flow preserves phase-space volume. The theorem is MA.O.A4; its physical use is here.

objects.label: Rigid-body motion, oscillators and small vibrations.
objects.text: PH.O.A1.1.3 Rigid-body motion, oscillators and small vibrations.

objects.label: Classical fields
objects.text: PH.O.A1.2 Classical fields. Maxwell's equations govern electromagnetic fields in vacuum, and in linear media given constitutive relations.

objects.label: Electrostatics and magnetostatics, including the quasistatic circuit l
objects.text: PH.O.A1.2.1 Electrostatics and magnetostatics, including the quasistatic circuit laws (Kirchhoff) as the limit of slow change.

objects.label: Electromagnetic waves; c is the propagation speed in vacuum.
objects.text: PH.O.A1.2.2 Electromagnetic waves; c is the propagation speed in vacuum.

objects.label: Classical optics
objects.text: PH.O.A1.2.3 Classical optics: geometric optics in the short-wavelength limit; diffraction and interference.

objects.label: Special relativity
objects.text: PH.O.A1.3 Special relativity. The laws take the same form in all inertial frames, and c is frame-invariant.

objects.label: Lorentz transformations; time dilation; length contraction.
objects.text: PH.O.A1.3.1 Lorentz transformations; time dilation; length contraction.

objects.label: Mass–energy equivalence, E = mc² for a body at rest.
objects.text: PH.O.A1.3.2 Mass–energy equivalence, E = mc² for a body at rest.

objects.label: Symmetry and conservation
objects.text: PH.O.A1.4 Symmetry and conservation. Noether: each continuous symmetry of a local action yields a conserved current. The theorem is MA (uses MA.O.A4); the physical conservation law is PH.

objects.label: Energy, momentum and angular momentum from time, space and rotation sy
objects.text: PH.O.A1.4.1 Energy, momentum and angular momentum from time, space and rotation symmetry.

objects.label: Charge conservation from the gauge symmetry of electrodynamics.
objects.text: PH.O.A1.4.2 Charge conservation from the gauge symmetry of electrodynamics.

objects.label: Continuum mechanics
objects.text: PH.O.A1.5 Continuum mechanics. Solids and fluids are treated as continua where the medium is smooth on the scale of interest. Cauchy stress gives traction t = σᵀn.

objects.label: Linear elasticity
objects.text: PH.O.A1.5.1 Linear elasticity: Hooke's law for small strain in a linear elastic solid.

objects.label: Constitutive laws close the balance equations
objects.text: PH.O.A1.5.2 Constitutive laws close the balance equations. The artefact meeting a specification is EN.

objects.label: Quantum systems
objects.text: PH.O.A2 Quantum systems

objects.label: States and dynamics
objects.text: PH.O.A2.1 States and dynamics. A closed system's state evolves unitarily by the Schrödinger equation. The Born rule gives outcome probabilities.

objects.label: The uncertainty relation σ_x σ_p ≥ ħ/2 holds for any state (the theore
objects.text: PH.O.A2.1.1 The uncertainty relation σ_x σ_p ≥ ħ/2 holds for any state (the theorem is MA.O.A2, as operator algebra).

objects.label: Decoherence
objects.text: PH.O.A2.1.2 Decoherence: interaction with an environment suppresses interference in a preferred basis. It does not by itself select a single outcome.

objects.label: Tunnelling and bound states.
objects.text: PH.O.A2.1.3 Tunnelling and bound states.

objects.label: Non-locality
objects.text: PH.O.A2.2 Non-locality. Bell: any local hidden-variable theory with measurement independence obeys the CHSH bound S ≤ 2. Quantum mechanics reaches 2√2 (the Tsirelson bound). Loophole-free violations were reported in 2015 (Delft, Vienna, NIST).

objects.label: Entanglement as a resource
objects.text: PH.O.A2.2.1 Entanglement as a resource: teleportation, quantum key distribution. Deployed protocols are CS.O.A5.

objects.label: No-signalling
objects.text: PH.O.A2.2.2 No-signalling: entanglement cannot transmit information faster than light.

objects.label: Quantum fields and particles
objects.text: PH.O.A2.3 Quantum fields and particles. The Standard Model describes three of the four known interactions, with gauge group SU(3)×SU(2)×U(1).

objects.label: Spin–statistics and CPT hold for local, Lorentz-invariant quantum fiel
objects.text: PH.O.A2.3.1 Spin–statistics and CPT hold for local, Lorentz-invariant quantum field theories with energy bounded below.

objects.label: The Higgs boson was observed in 2012 (ATLAS and CMS).
objects.text: PH.O.A2.3.2 The Higgs boson was observed in 2012 (ATLAS and CMS).

objects.label: Neutrino oscillation implies non-zero neutrino masses
objects.text: PH.O.A2.3.3 Neutrino oscillation implies non-zero neutrino masses. The mass ordering is OPEN.

objects.label: Renormalisation
objects.text: PH.O.A2.3.4 Renormalisation: physics at low energy is insensitive to most details at high energy, for renormalisable theories and effective field theories.

objects.label: Atomic, molecular and optical physics
objects.text: PH.O.A2.4 Atomic, molecular and optical physics. Atomic level structure, spectra, and the interaction of light with atoms. The chemical bond is CH; PH owns the level structure.

objects.label: Lasers
objects.text: PH.O.A2.4.1 Lasers: stimulated emission in a medium with population inversion.

objects.label: Laser cooling and Bose–Einstein condensation of dilute gases (first ac
objects.text: PH.O.A2.4.2 Laser cooling and Bose–Einstein condensation of dilute gases (first achieved 1995).

objects.label: Atomic clocks and precision measurement
objects.text: PH.O.A2.4.3 Atomic clocks and precision measurement. The SI second has been defined by the caesium-133 hyperfine transition since 1967.

objects.label: Interpretation of quantum mechanics
objects.text: PH.O.A2.5 Interpretation of quantum mechanics. CONTESTED placement. The empirical content stays here. Copenhagen, many-worlds, pilot-wave and collapse theories, as arguments, are PL.

objects.label: Gravitation and the cosmos
objects.text: PH.O.A3 Gravitation and the cosmos

objects.label: Newtonian gravity
objects.text: PH.O.A3.1 Newtonian gravity. The inverse-square attraction is valid for weak fields and speeds much below c.

objects.label: Kepler's laws follow for two point masses.
objects.text: PH.O.A3.1.1 Kepler's laws follow for two point masses.

objects.label: Celestial mechanics
objects.text: PH.O.A3.1.2 Celestial mechanics: perturbation theory for many bodies. The n-body problem's mathematics is MA.O.A4.

objects.label: General relativity
objects.text: PH.O.A3.2 General relativity. Einstein's field equations relate spacetime curvature to stress-energy. The equivalence principle holds locally.

objects.label: Classical tests
objects.text: PH.O.A3.2.1 Classical tests: Mercury's perihelion, light deflection, gravitational redshift.

objects.label: Black holes
objects.text: PH.O.A3.2.2 Black holes: the Schwarzschild and Kerr solutions. Singularity theorems (Penrose, Hawking) assume energy conditions and trapped surfaces (uses MA.O.A3).

objects.label: Gravitational waves
objects.text: PH.O.A3.2.3 Gravitational waves: first detected 14 September 2015, announced February 2016 (LIGO).

objects.label: Astrophysics
objects.text: PH.O.A3.3 Astrophysics. Stars, compact objects, galaxies.

objects.label: Stellar structure and nucleosynthesis.
objects.text: PH.O.A3.3.1 Stellar structure and nucleosynthesis.

objects.label: The Chandrasekhar limit
objects.text: PH.O.A3.3.2 The Chandrasekhar limit: about 1.4 solar masses for a non-rotating white dwarf supported by electron degeneracy pressure.

objects.label: Neutron stars, pulsars, accretion.
objects.text: PH.O.A3.3.3 Neutron stars, pulsars, accretion.

objects.label: Cosmology
objects.text: PH.O.A3.4 Cosmology. ΛCDM fits the expansion history, the cosmic microwave background and large-scale structure.

objects.label: Hubble–Lemaître expansion
objects.text: PH.O.A3.4.1 Hubble–Lemaître expansion. The "Hubble tension" between early- and late-universe measurements is OPEN.

objects.label: The CMB, discovered 1965.
objects.text: PH.O.A3.4.2 The CMB, discovered 1965.

objects.label: Dark matter and dark energy
objects.text: PH.O.A3.4.3 Dark matter and dark energy: inferred from gravity; their identities are OPEN.

objects.label: Inflation
objects.text: PH.O.A3.4.4 Inflation: a CONTESTED programme with supporting but not decisive evidence.

objects.label: Quantum gravity
objects.text: PH.O.A3.5 Quantum gravity. OPEN.

objects.label: Bekenstein–Hawking entropy S = k_B c³ A / (4Għ) for a black hole of ho
objects.text: PH.O.A3.5.1 Bekenstein–Hawking entropy S = k_B c³ A / (4Għ) for a black hole of horizon area A. (The v1 omission of k_B is fixed.)

objects.label: Hawking radiation
objects.text: PH.O.A3.5.2 Hawking radiation: a semiclassical prediction (quantum fields on a curved background), not yet observed for astrophysical black holes.

objects.label: Programmes
objects.text: PH.O.A3.5.3 Programmes: string theory, loop quantum gravity, asymptotic safety. All lack decisive empirical tests.

objects.label: Matter in equilibrium
objects.text: PH.O.A4 Matter in equilibrium

objects.label: Thermodynamics.
objects.text: PH.O.A4.1 Thermodynamics.

objects.label: First law
objects.text: PH.O.A4.1.1 First law: the change in internal energy of a closed system equals heat in minus work out (sign convention stated).

objects.label: Second law
objects.text: PH.O.A4.1.2 Second law: the entropy of an isolated system does not decrease. Carnot efficiency 1 − T_c/T_h bounds any engine between two reservoirs.

objects.label: Third law
objects.text: PH.O.A4.1.3 Third law: entropy approaches a constant as T → 0, for systems with a non-degenerate ground state.

objects.label: Statistical mechanics
objects.text: PH.O.A4.2 Statistical mechanics. Ensembles derive thermodynamics from microstates. The microcanonical ensemble assumes equilibrium and equal a priori probability.

objects.label: Boltzmann entropy S = k_B ln W.
objects.text: PH.O.A4.2.1 Boltzmann entropy S = k_B ln W.

objects.label: Quantum statistics
objects.text: PH.O.A4.2.2 Quantum statistics: Fermi–Dirac and Bose–Einstein distributions for indistinguishable particles.

objects.label: Ergodic hypothesis
objects.text: PH.O.A4.2.3 Ergodic hypothesis: CONTESTED as a justification. The ergodic theorems are MA.O.A4.

objects.label: Phase transitions.
objects.text: PH.O.A4.3 Phase transitions.

objects.label: Clapeyron equation
objects.text: PH.O.A4.3.1 Clapeyron equation: dP/dT = L/(T Δv) on a coexistence line.

objects.label: Clausius–Clapeyron
objects.text: PH.O.A4.3.2 Clausius–Clapeyron: d ln P/dT = L/(RT²). It adds an ideal vapour, negligible condensed-phase volume and constant L. (The v1 mislabel is fixed.)

objects.label: Critical phenomena and universality
objects.text: PH.O.A4.3.3 Critical phenomena and universality: systems with the same dimension, symmetry and interaction range share critical exponents. Renormalisation-group explanation (Wilson).

objects.label: Mermin–Wagner
objects.text: PH.O.A4.3.4 Mermin–Wagner: no spontaneous breaking of a continuous symmetry at T > 0 in d ≤ 2 with short-range interactions.

objects.label: Condensed states
objects.text: PH.O.A4.4 Condensed states. Band structure, superconductivity, magnetism, topological phases, defects.

objects.label: Quasiparticles
objects.text: PH.O.A4.4.1 Quasiparticles: an excitation with decay rate Γ = 1/τ is well defined when ħΓ is much less than its energy. (The v1 lifetime–rate confusion is fixed.)

objects.label: BCS theory of conventional superconductivity
objects.text: PH.O.A4.4.2 BCS theory of conventional superconductivity: electron pairing mediated by phonons, for weak coupling. High-temperature superconductivity mechanisms are OPEN.

objects.label: Semiconductors and device physics
objects.text: PH.O.A4.4.3 Semiconductors and device physics: drift–diffusion transport in the low-injection regime.

objects.label: Dislocations as the mechanism of plastic flow in crystals.
objects.text: PH.O.A4.4.4 Dislocations as the mechanism of plastic flow in crystals.

objects.label: Topological phases
objects.text: PH.O.A4.4.5 Topological phases: quantum Hall effects (integer 1980, fractional 1982).

objects.label: Matter out of equilibrium
objects.text: PH.O.A5 Matter out of equilibrium

objects.label: Transport near equilibrium.
objects.text: PH.O.A5.1 Transport near equilibrium.

objects.label: Linear response; the fluctuation–dissipation theorem for systems near
objects.text: PH.O.A5.1.1 Linear response; the fluctuation–dissipation theorem for systems near equilibrium.

objects.label: Onsager reciprocity
objects.text: PH.O.A5.1.2 Onsager reciprocity: assumes microscopic reversibility, with the magnetic field reversed when one is present.

objects.label: Diffusion, conduction, viscosity as transport coefficients; Boltzmann
objects.text: PH.O.A5.1.3 Diffusion, conduction, viscosity as transport coefficients; Boltzmann transport equation for dilute gases.

objects.label: Fluids
objects.text: PH.O.A5.2 Fluids. Navier–Stokes governs Newtonian fluids. Global smoothness in three dimensions is OPEN and owned by MA.O.A4.

objects.label: Turbulence
objects.text: PH.O.A5.2.1 Turbulence: Kolmogorov's 1941 scaling for homogeneous isotropic turbulence at high Reynolds number. A full theory is OPEN.

objects.label: Dimensionless groups (Reynolds, Mach) set the regime.
objects.text: PH.O.A5.2.2 Dimensionless groups (Reynolds, Mach) set the regime.

objects.label: Plasmas
objects.text: PH.O.A5.3 Plasmas. Quasi-neutral ionised matter, collective behaviour on scales larger than the Debye length.

objects.label: Magnetohydrodynamics, valid where collisions keep a fluid description.
objects.text: PH.O.A5.3.1 Magnetohydrodynamics, valid where collisions keep a fluid description.

objects.label: Fusion plasmas
objects.text: PH.O.A5.3.2 Fusion plasmas: Lawson criterion for net energy gain, given confinement time and density at a stated temperature.

objects.label: Radiation and matter.
objects.text: PH.O.A5.4 Radiation and matter.

objects.label: Planck's law for blackbody radiation in thermal equilibrium; Stefan–Bo
objects.text: PH.O.A5.4.1 Planck's law for blackbody radiation in thermal equilibrium; Stefan–Boltzmann law as its integral.

objects.label: Radiative transfer through absorbing and emitting media.
objects.text: PH.O.A5.4.2 Radiative transfer through absorbing and emitting media.

objects.label: Nuclear decay and radiation interaction with matter
objects.text: PH.O.A5.4.3 Interaction of ionising radiation with matter (stopping, attenuation). Nuclear decay itself, with its half-lives, moved to PH.O.A2.3.5 after the pilot (claim 38).

objects.label: Nonlinear dynamics and complex systems
objects.text: PH.O.A5.5 Nonlinear dynamics and complex systems. Sensitive dependence on initial conditions; pattern formation; active matter. Theorems are MA.O.A4; the physical system is here.

objects.label: Non-equilibrium fluctuation theorems (Jarzynski, Crooks) for systems d
objects.text: PH.O.A5.5.1 Non-equilibrium fluctuation theorems (Jarzynski, Crooks) for systems driven from an initial equilibrium.

methods.label: Formulate
methods.example: write the Lagrangian; choose units and variables

methods.label: Solve
methods.example: perturbation theory, exact solution, symmetry argument

methods.label: Simulate
methods.example: lattice QCD, molecular dynamics, N-body, plasma codes

warrants.standard: prediction matches measurement within stated uncertainty; derivation valid
warrants.defeaters: regime exceeded (speed near c, action near ħ)

warrants.standard: controlled experiment with quoted uncertainty; replication; 5σ for discovery claims in particle physics
observation with stated uncertainty; independent probes agree
warrants.defeaters: model dependence, selection effects, cosmic variance

warrants.standard: internal consistency; no empirical warrant yet
measured property matches a derived value
measurement, or simulation with an error bound

sections.governing_thought:
Physics is exhausted by four faces of one pyramid: objects, methods, warrants and bridges.
Its objects divide into five regimes: classical motion and fields, quantum systems, gravitation and the cosmos, matter in equilibrium, and matter out of equilibrium.
sections.key_line:
Dimension: **the governing constants of the claim** (which of c, ħ, G and N set its scale). Logic inductive. Order: structural, from fewest constants to most, then the N axis.
1. Classical motion and fields
2. Quantum systems
3. Gravitation and the cosmos
4. Matter in equilibrium
5. Matter out of equilibrium

**Cube map.** This is an adaptation of the c–G–ħ cube of physical theories. It is not Bronstein's 1933 scheme, and the attribution of the cube's modern form is left open (UNVERIFIED). N is the author's axis.

| Vertex | Theory | Home |
|---|---|---|
| none | Newtonian mechanics | PH.O.A1.1 |
| c | special relativity; Maxwell electrodynamics | PH.O.A1.2–A1.3 |
| ħ | non-relativistic quantum mechanics | PH.O.A2.1 |
| c, ħ | quantum field theory | PH.O.A2.3 |
| G | Newtonian gravity | PH.O.A3.1 |
| c, G | general relativity | PH.O.A3.2 |
| G, ħ | no established theory | REFUSED as a cell. Such claims go to PH.O.A3.5, OPEN |
| c, G, ħ | quantum gravity | PH.O.A3.5, OPEN |
| N, equilibrium | thermodynamics, statistical mechanics, condensed matter | PH.O.A4 |
| N, driven or relaxing | transport, fluids, plasma, radiation in matter, nonlinear dynamics | PH.O.A5 |

**MECE test.** Exclusive: each claim is placed by the largest set of constants its derivation needs. Exhaustive: every vertex of the cube, and both states of the N axis, has a home or a stated refusal.
**CONTESTED.** Newtonian gravity is placed in A3, not A1, so all gravitation shares one home. The alternative files it in A1 by the "no c, no ħ" rule.
sections.assignment_rules:
1. Place a claim by the largest set of constants its derivation needs. Place N-body claims in A4 or A5 by equilibrium.
2. A theorem about the equations is MA. The claim that nature obeys them is PH.
3. A bond, reaction rate or molecular structure is CH. Atomic levels are PH.
4. A device meeting a specification is EN. The law it relies on is PH.
5. Quantum interpretation: empirical content in PH.O.A2, argument in PL.
6. Physics education research is ED (uses PH).
7. Climate and Earth-system claims are EA. The radiative law they use is PH.O.A5.4.
8. A claim that crosses regimes goes to the regime with more constants.

**PhySH** (APS) has five facets: research areas, physical systems, properties, techniques and professional topics. It lists 17 disciplines (checked: Wikipedia summary of physh.aps.org). The 17 names are not yet transcribed, so a discipline-by-discipline map is pending (R4 partial). Professional topics such as education and careers are refused to ED and BU.
sections.validation:
Sizes: key line 5. Face O 5 cells + 24 sub-cells = 29, with 65 named objects below them. M roles 5. Heuristics 7, outside the count. W rows 6. B bridges 8.
Key line, word for word: Classical motion and fields. Quantum systems. Gravitation and the cosmos. Matter in equilibrium. Matter out of equilibrium.
OPEN: quantum gravity (A3.5); dark matter and dark energy; the Hubble tension; neutrino mass ordering; high-temperature superconductivity; turbulence; 3D Navier–Stokes smoothness (MA, cited).
CONTESTED: interpretation of QM (PH vs PL); Newtonian gravity in A3 rather than A1; inflation; naturalness as a guide; the ergodic justification.
Fixed from the audit: the cube is now named as an adaptation; N is marked as the author's axis; G–ħ is refused and c–G–ħ is OPEN; transport, plasma and radiation have homes; Clapeyron is distinguished from Clausius–Clapeyron; the quasiparticle condition uses rate; k_B is restored; heuristics are outside the count.
